Title: EVT-OP-012: Hammersley–Clifford for extremal graphical models on non-decomposable graphs
Labels: open-problem, area:multivariate, type:research, difficulty:hard, status:research

**Status in the survey:** OPEN-EXPLICIT in 2020, likely resolved: Engelke, Ivanovs and Strokorb (AAP 2025) prove a Hammersley–Clifford-type theorem, but the survey did not verify that it settles homogeneity.

## Source and quote
Engelke and Hitz, JRSSB 2020, arXiv:1812.01734, Remark 2:

> it is an open problem whether they can be chosen to be homogeneous

The quote was extracted from the source text, with symbols flattened; check it against the published version before citing.

## Why it matters
River-network flood models (`graphicalExtremes`).

## What the library already has
Multivariate regular variation, exponent measures, the multivariate GPD and spectral measures.

## What is missing
Densities of exponent measures and any graph theory. The survey rates reach as low.

## Pointers
`docs/PRACTICAL_OPEN_PROBLEMS.md`, C12. Survey feasibility estimates are unchecked plans, not results.
